title: Two-Phase Object Initialization (Initialize Separate from Constructor)
pattern: An object's constructor leaves the instance in an invalid or incomplete state, requiring the caller to explicitly call a separate `.initialize()` or `.init()` routine before using it.
why_bad: Exposes the system to uninitialized state bugs. A consumer might call a routine before initializing, violating class invariants and causing crashes, null-pointer dereferences, or logical errors.
detection: The constructor returns an object containing uninitialized or default/null fields that must be populated by an explicit, secondary init routine before other member functions are valid.
counterexample: Types representing lazy resources that connect/initialize transparently on first actual method invocation.
fix: Perform all required initialization directly inside the constructor (`new`), returning a fully initialized, valid, ready-to-use object.
